prompt: What does it mean for a problem to be NP-hard but not necessarily in NP?
options: Every NP problem reduces to it in polynomial time, but its own solutions may not be verifiable in polynomial time
It has already been proven unsolvable
It is automatically also in P
explanation: NP-hard only requires being 'at least as hard as' every NP problem via reduction — it doesn't require membership in NP itself. NP-complete = NP-hard AND in NP.

prompt: What is the standard two-step approach to prove a new problem X is NP-complete?
acceptedAnswers: show x is in np and reduce a known np-complete problem to x
prove np membership and reduce from a known np-complete problem
explanation: 1) Show X ∈ NP (a solution can be checked in poly time). 2) Show a known NP-complete problem reduces to X in poly time.
